# Dream Maker

> A local-first workbench that turns a vague idea into a frozen, testable specification, then
> hands it to four role agents (Seeker, Planner, Executor, Reviewer) that plan, build and review
> the result. Runs on 127.0.0.1, stores data in a SQLite file next to the executable, and refuses
> every paid model call by default.

## What it is

Dream Maker is a desktop application for Windows. You describe what you want in plain language.
A role called the Seeker interviews you until the idea becomes explicit, testable requirements
with acceptance criteria. You confirm the requirements. Only then do the engineering roles run:
a Planner designs tasks bound to requirement ids, an Executor builds inside a leased workspace,
and a Reviewer checks the produced tree hash against the frozen spec. If the Reviewer finds a gap,
the result returns to the Seeker, which asks you about that specific blocker.

## Key facts

- Written in TypeScript (server and web) plus a small Go launcher, runs on Node 22.16 or later.
- Binds to 127.0.0.1 only. There is no cloud mode and no multi-tenant mode.
- Data is a SQLite file at data/<product>/dream-maker.sqlite inside the application folder.
- Two products share one binary: dream-maker.exe (Dream Maker) and dream-maker.exe df (DreamFlow).
- Six harness lanes: dsh, claude, codex, pi, opencode, cline, routed through a local Magpie gateway.
- Zero-usage by default: paid model dispatch is refused before any network call.
- Licensing: MIT.

## Who it is for

Developers and technical founders who want an AI coding workflow that cannot silently build the
wrong thing. It is not a hosted service and it does not include model credits.

## What it is not

- Not a cloud IDE and not a hosted agent platform.
- Not a wrapper around a single provider; harnesses are interchangeable.
- Not finished. The roadmap file lists what is missing.
